title: Verification & External Tools
description: Study executable verification, unit tests and counterexamples, verifier reliability, and evidence and concise explanations. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Executable verification
lessons.description: Design input checks before accepting the computed result.
lessons.conceptOverview: Use calculations, tests or solvers to check claims when the task has a precise criterion. Tool output is evidence only if inputs, units and execution context are correct.
lessons.whyItMatters: Correct execution does not repair incorrect inputs.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Use calculations, tests or solvers to check claims when the task has a precise criterion. Tool output is evidence only if inputs, units and execution context are correct.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Use calculations, tests or solvers to check claims when the task has a precise criterion. Tool output is evidence only if inputs, units and execution context are correct.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A calculator returns a correct value for a mistyped interest rate.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Design input checks before accepting the computed result. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Correct execution does not repair incorrect inputs.
commonMistakes: A calculator result is always the answer to the user's intended question.

lessons.title: Unit tests and counterexamples
lessons.description: Add boundary tests and explain what they establish.
lessons.conceptOverview: A counterexample disproves a universal claim, while a passing finite test set gives limited support. Choose boundary and adversarial cases that challenge the proposed rule.
lessons.whyItMatters: Tests should challenge boundaries and claimed generality.

lessons.title: Verifier reliability
lessons.description: Strengthen the grader with behavioral cases and inspect false positives.
lessons.conceptOverview: A verifier can be incomplete or wrong. Evaluate false acceptance and false rejection, and prefer independent checks when consequences are high.
lessons.whyItMatters: Verification quality limits the reliability of accepted solutions.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A verifier can be incomplete or wrong. Evaluate false acceptance and false rejection, and prefer independent checks when consequences are high.

sections.content: A verifier can be incomplete or wrong. Evaluate false acceptance and false rejection, and prefer independent checks when consequences are high.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A code grader checks only the return type, allowing an incorrect constant answer to pass.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Strengthen the grader with behavioral cases and inspect false positives. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Verification quality limits the reliability of accepted solutions.
commonMistakes: Any automated grader is an infallible correctness oracle.

lessons.title: Evidence and concise explanations
lessons.description: Validate the result directly and present the decisive check.
lessons.conceptOverview: A useful explanation presents checkable steps, assumptions and supporting evidence. Length or apparent confidence is not a correctness measure, and explanations may not faithfully reveal internal computation.
lessons.whyItMatters: Checkable evidence matters more than explanation length.
